I read the whole file (lines 1–252). It has no @[simp] attributes and no simp sets of its own. Its simp calls are all `simp only` with explicit lemma lists, either on the file's own private lemmas (`c1L_h_fst`, `c1L_h_snd`) or on Mathlib categorical lemmas (`Category.assoc`, `pullback.lift_fst`, `CommRingCat.hom_comp`, `RingHom.comp_apply`). The two plain `simp only [RingHom.comp_apply] at hxy` uses are one-off.

The file's rewriting lemmas are `c1L_φ_apply` (proved by rfl), `c1L_germ_φ0Hom`, `c1L_φ0Hom_germ`, `c1L_h_fst`, `c1L_h_snd` and `c1L_h_genericPoint`. All are private and are used only through targeted `rw` or `exact` in this file. I found no competing rules, no unwanted expansion and no plausible rewrite cycle. Making any of these `@[simp]` would not clearly help. Their left-hand sides depend on heavy dependent arguments such as `hU` membership proofs and `IsIntegral` instances. They are used once each, and a global simp attribute on a private one-off helper adds no practical value.

I did not run Lean, so this is a judgement from reading the source. The remaining uncertainty is that I did not check how the imported Definitions files set up simp for `DRModelPackageLevel`.
